what: Atlassian makes software for teams: Jira for tracking work, Confluence for documentation, and tools for IT service management. Most of its customers find it and buy it without ever speaking to a salesperson.
customers: Software development teams, IT departments and increasingly business teams, in over 300,000 organisations.
money: cloud subscriptions to Jira, Confluence and related products
a share of third-party apps sold for its platform
moat: Jira holds the record of how work gets done inside an engineering organisation, and the processes, integrations and history built around it make replacing it painful.
risks: Operating margin is near zero because stock-based compensation is very large
Migrating customers from server products to cloud is a long transition
Competition in work management is crowded
opportunities: Revenue grew about 26% last year with an 85% gross margin
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Selling to IT service management and business teams expands beyond its engineering base
watch: Cloud revenue growth and free cash flow margin.
